Aatrox.combo: For a basic trade, hit Aatrox twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. To start a fight, use the first Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build Heat into the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you can cut off Aatrox’s escape route, block it with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Aatrox.laning: Early on, focus on farming without giving Aatrox a kill, and safely chip away at his health with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. When Aatrox steps forward to last-hit, hit him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and follow with Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you push the lane too far, check river vision; if you have no vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Aatrox.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade and Aatrox W Infernal Chains. If Aatrox P Deathbringer Stance, Aatrox E Umbral Dash, and Aatrox R World Ender keep healing him during a duel, reduce his healing with Morellonomicon.
Aatrox.escape: Right after you make Aatrox use Aatrox E Umbral Dash, Rumble has an opportunity to close the gap. If Aatrox W Infernal Chains catches you, don’t engage; use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed to leave the area immediately. Keep your distance while Aatrox R World Ender is active, then fight again after it expires.
Aatrox.fight: Look for a short trade right after Aatrox uses the empowered basic attack from Aatrox P Deathbringer Stance on a minion.
Aatrox.phase: Early on, focus on farming without giving Aatrox a kill. Later, avoid forcing close fights because it will be difficult to get on top of him.
Aatrox.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and find a position where Rumble Q Flamespitter can hit several enemies in their frontline. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. Use Rumble R The Equalizer to split their frontline from their backline or block their escape route in a fight that has already started.
Aatrox.watch: Aatrox Q The Darkin Blade deals his main damage and can knock you up, so watch the cast and dodge toward the area just inside or outside the blade’s edge. If Aatrox W Infernal Chains hits you, walk out of its area immediately and use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed to escape.

Kled.escape: Look to engage after Kled E Jousting has been used and before Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! comes back up. If you're caught by Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope, immediately use Rumble W Scrap Shield's movement speed to create distance before it pulls you in. If you can't get away, move toward a minion wave or your allies to make it harder for Kled to follow.
Kled.build: Build armor first against Kled's main damage. Rumble has no mobility skill and is easy to lock down with Kled's crowd control, so you can also prioritize tenacity. If you build a lot of health alone, the max-health damage from Kled W Violent Tendencies and Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! will also be higher.
Kled.combo: Your basic trade is to hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to amplify its slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on. For a full fight, manage your heat so Rumble E Electro Harpoon puts you in the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If Rumble R The Equalizer is available, cut off Kled's escape route, follow with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then hit him with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Kled.fight: Safely poke with Rumble E Electro Harpoon first. When Kled steps up to last-hit, slow him to get within range of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Avoid extended fights when Kled W Violent Tendencies is ready or he can use a catching ability. Before getting close, check your heat, then use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield.
Kled.laning: Keep your distance to avoid being caught by Kled first, and save one cast of Rumble E Electro Harpoon. If you can't finish him for certain after knocking Kled off Skaarl, create distance to reduce his opportunities to build Courage, and push him out of lane if possible so he can't kill minions. If you've pushed the lane too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to disengage.
Kled.phase: Early on, watch out for Kled's engage and catching abilities, but Rumble can take trades against physical melee opponents reasonably well. In the late game, Rumble can have trouble getting close and can be killed, so avoid reckless engages.
Kled.teamfight: Keep vision on the flanks to prepare for Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!!'s long-range engage. If you can't stop it, hold your formation behind your allied frontline, and use Rumble R The Equalizer to split the enemy frontline and backline or block their escape route. Rumble uses Rumble Q Flamespitter to hit multiple targets together in front of the frontline and lowers magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon.
Kled.watch: If you're caught by Kled Q Bear Trap on a Rope, immediately create distance before it pulls you in. When Kled W Violent Tendencies is active, back off to avoid taking the max-health damage from his fourth attack, then get close again. Kled E Jousting and Kled R Chaaaaaaaarge!!! are also ways for him to engage, so don't assume you're safe just because one is down.

Aurora.phase: Early on, play safely against Aurora’s magic damage because Rumble has low magic resistance. Later, Rumble can be killed quickly if he can’t get on top of her, so fight behind your frontline instead of chasing Aurora alone.
Aurora.teamfight: From behind your frontline, find a position where several enemies can be hit by Rumble Q Flamespitter, and lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. Cast Rumble R The Equalizer between their frontline and backline or across their retreat path to block movement. If Aurora jumps in but has not scored a takedown, look for a chance to catch her; when retreating, don’t leave low-health allies behind.
Aurora.build: Aurora’s main damage is magic and Rumble has low magic resistance, so buy a Null-Magic Mantle first. Choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots and fit Force of Nature between your core items to gain more time on top of her. If healing from Aurora P Spirit Abjuration offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, reduce her healing with Morellonomicon.
Aurora.combo: For a basic trade, hit Aurora twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter active. To start a fight, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build Heat into the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you can see Aurora’s escape route, block it with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Aurora.escape: Don’t engage just because Aurora E The Weirding is down; wait for the opening after she has also used Aurora W Across the Veil. If health has decreased while under the curse from Aurora Q Twofold Hex, stop engaging and retreat with Rumble W Scrap Shield’s shield and movement speed.
Aurora.fight: When Aurora steps forward to last-hit, slow her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then get into range for Rumble Q Flamespitter. If Aurora E The Weirding or Aurora W Across the Veil is still available, don’t chase recklessly; make her use a mobility ability, then look for another chance to get on top of her. Once you’re on her, turn Rumble Q Flamespitter to keep Aurora in its area.
Aurora.laning: Early on, Aurora’s magic damage is dangerous, so poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. If you push the lane too far, check river vision; in areas without vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Aurora.watch: Aurora Q Twofold Hex damages again when the curse is recalled, and deals more damage the more health you have lost. If you are cursed, move out of the line between Aurora and yourself; if you are below half health, retreat before the curse is recalled. Once Aurora R Between Worlds appears, leaving it slows you, so decide before she casts whether to retreat or fight inside it.

Camille.build: Build armor first to counter Camille’s main damage. Armor won’t reduce the true damage from Camille Q Precision Protocol, and Camille W Tactical Sweep scales with your max health, so armor or health alone can’t block all her damage. If healing from Camille W Tactical Sweep offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, reduce her healing with Morellonomicon.
Camille.combo: Manage your Heat: slow Camille with the first Rumble E Electro Harpoon, hit her with the second, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter in the Danger Zone and move to keep her in its area. If you have your ultimate, cut off Camille’s escape route with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Camille.escape: After the stun and dash from Camille E Hookshot are down, use the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon to get on top of her. If Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum is still available, don’t go deep just because Camille E Hookshot is down. Use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed to close in during the window after Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum is also down.
Camille.fight: Avoid trading right after Camille P Adaptive Defenses activates its shield; fight after the shield has been removed. Slow her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then keep her within Rumble Q Flamespitter’s range when she steps forward to last-hit.
Camille.laning: Stand between minions and away from walls to reduce Camille E Hookshot’s engage angles, and poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Take control of the lane before Camille’s first core item comes online, but check river vision if you push too far. In areas without vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Camille.phase: Early on, Camille has weak stats and poor wave clear, so take control with Rumble E Electro Harpoon poke before her first core item. Later, Rumble has trouble getting on top of her, so don’t force an engage; also don’t leave a side lane open where Camille can quickly take down a turret.
Camille.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and position in front of the enemy frontline so Rumble Q Flamespitter can hit several targets. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. When a fight breaks out, cast Rumble R The Equalizer between their frontline and backline or across their escape route to block their movement.
Camille.watch: Camille E Hookshot uses walls to engage from long range and stun you, so stand away from walls. Don’t use a counter ability at the moment Camille R The Hextech Ultimatum engages; instead, keep your distance by dodging Camille W Tactical Sweep or Camille E Hookshot beforehand.

Akali.fight: When Akali steps forward to last-hit or comes out of Akali W Twilight Shroud to engage, slow her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and fight back. Don’t chase far if Akali E Shuriken Flip and Akali W Twilight Shroud are still available. When you get on top of her, watch your Heat and use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s shield and movement speed.
Akali.build: Survive early with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury’s Treads for your boots. Since Akali’s main damage is magic, build magic resistance first; if you need more time to stay on top of her, fit Force of Nature between your core items. Akali also tends to have high magic resistance, so add penetration to Rumble’s magic damage.
Akali.combo: For a basic trade, hit Akali twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter active for its full duration. In fights, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build Heat into the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you have an angle to cut off Akali’s escape route, cast Rumble R The Equalizer first, then follow with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Akali.escape: Don’t rush the chase if only one of the two is down, since the remaining option can still be used to escape. The window before Akali R Perfect Execution is available again is a chance to build a lead in health and CS.
Akali.laning: Rumble is vulnerable to magic damage early, so poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. If you push the lane too far, check river vision; where you have no vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Akali.phase: Later, avoid forcing an engage because Rumble can have trouble getting on top of her and can be killed quickly.
Akali.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and position in front of the enemy frontline so Rumble Q Flamespitter can hit several targets. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. Cast Rumble R The Equalizer between their frontline and backline, or across the escape route in a fight that has already started, to block their movement.

Renekton.escape: Right after Renekton E Slice and Dice is down—especially after he uses it to disengage—is your window to close the gap. When backing off after his combo, move in a direction that gives Renekton no foothold for a second dash.
Renekton.build: Renekton’s main damage is physical, so build armor first. However, armor won’t block the magic damage from Renekton R Dominus, and empowered Renekton E Slice and Dice reduces your armor, so prioritize positioning that lets you dodge his dash. If the healing from Renekton Q Cull the Meek offsets the damage over time from Rumble Q Flamespitter, reduce his healing with Morellonomicon.
Renekton.combo: When Renekton has no Fury or Renekton E Slice and Dice is down, hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on him. For an extended fight, use the first harpoon to build Heat into the Danger Zone, then activate Q and turn as you move to keep Renekton in range. If Rumble R The Equalizer is available, cut off his escape, then follow with the harpoon slow and Q.
Renekton.fight: When Renekton has no Fury, poke first with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Only slow him as he steps up to last-hit, then move into Rumble Q Flamespitter range. Trade back after Renekton has used Q, W, and E, or right after Renekton E Slice and Dice is used to disengage. When his Fury is full, don’t rely on Rumble W Scrap Shield and go in first.
Renekton.laning: Don’t stand in or behind a minion wave, since it gives Renekton E Slice and Dice a platform to engage from. Reposition as needed and poke with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Poke when Renekton steps up to hit minions and build Fury. If you don’t have an angle to get close, don’t use Rumble Q Flamespitter first. If you’ve pushed the lane too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to disengage when vision is missing.
Renekton.phase: Rumble is strong in the mid game as his ability power builds, while Renekton’s value falls off from the mid game onward. Grow without giving up kills, and don’t force your way in late.
Renekton.teamfight: From behind your frontline, position so multiple enemies in their frontline are in the cone of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. Cast Rumble R The Equalizer between their frontline and backline, or along the escape route from a fight already underway, to restrict movement.
Renekton.watch: When Renekton P Reign of Anger is above half or just below it, stand out of range to avoid an empowered Renekton W Ruthless Predator. Empowered W breaks shields first, so don’t try to block the combo with Rumble W Scrap Shield.

Tryndamere.escape: The window to close the gap is right after you make Tryndamere use E Spinning Slash. If Tryndamere W Mocking Shout is also down, you can engage without worrying about its slow. When you need to retreat, walk backward while facing Tryndamere to avoid Tryndamere W Mocking Shout.
Tryndamere.build: Build armor first since Tryndamere’s main damage is physical. If his self-healing offsets the damage over time from Rumble Q Flamespitter, reduce his healing with Morellonomicon.
Tryndamere.fight: Right after Tryndamere E Spinning Slash is down, slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and close the gap. Use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield to get in, then keep turning to land Rumble Q Flamespitter after activating it. When Tryndamere R Undying Rage activates, back away and wait out its duration.
Tryndamere.phase: Early on, Rumble can take trades against physical melee opponents, but it is important to harass Tryndamere before he builds Fury. Later, Rumble can struggle to get close and is easy to kill, so don’t force a solo fight against Tryndamere.
Tryndamere.teamfight: From behind your frontline, catch multiple enemies in the cone of Rumble Q Flamespitter and lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Draw Rumble R The Equalizer between the enemy frontline and backline or across their escape route to block movement. If Tryndamere R Undying Rage is ready, don’t go alone to hold the side lane; bring more players or trade for an objective.
Tryndamere.watch: As Tryndamere builds P Battle Fury, his critical strikes become dangerous, so keep your distance while he hits minions to build Fury. If he dashes in with Tryndamere E Spinning Slash, use Rumble W Scrap Shield to manage the distance. While Tryndamere R Undying Rage is active, don’t pour in more damage and back away.
Tryndamere.combo: Your basic trade is to hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on. To start a fight, watch your heat, use one charge of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter the Danger Zone, then turn on Rumble Q Flamespitter. When using your ultimate, block his escape route with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Tryndamere.laning: If you’ve pushed the lane too far, check river vision, and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape when you lack vision.

Jayce.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and catch multiple enemies in Rumble Q Flamespitter’s area. Use Rumble R The Equalizer to split the enemy frontline from the backline or block their escape route in a fight that has already started. Close in when Jayce Q To the Skies! is down, and use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to lower magic resistance and help your allied mage deal damage.
Jayce.build: Use Null-Magic Mantle to withstand the early game and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first against Jayce’s main damage, but it will not block the physical damage from Jayce Q To the Skies! / Shock Blast. Jayce E Thundering Blow / Acceleration Gate scales with maximum health, so use movement speed to leave telegraphed areas instead of greatly stacking health alone.
Jayce.combo: For a standard trade, hit both shots of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to stack the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on him. In a fight, check your Heat, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If your ultimate is available, cut off Jayce’s escape route with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and hit him with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Jayce.escape: The moment after Jayce leaps with Jayce Q To the Skies! is your chance to close the distance. If Jayce E Thundering Blow’s knockback is also down, slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and close in with Rumble W Scrap Shield. Do not force Rumble Q Flamespitter’s short range while both skills are still available.
Jayce.fight: When Jayce has his cannon out, poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon; when he steps forward to last-hit, land the slow and close in. After Jayce Q To the Skies!’s leap and Jayce E Thundering Blow’s knockback are down, close the distance with Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed. Check your Heat and leave room to activate Rumble Q Flamespitter in Danger Zone.
Jayce.laning: Against Jayce’s early pressure, farm defensively while moving side to side to dodge Jayce Q Shock Blast. If you have no opening to close in, do not use Rumble Q Flamespitter first; poke with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. If you have pushed too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape when there is no vision.
Jayce.phase: Jayce is strong early, so if you fall behind, farm defensively instead of forcing a comeback. In late game, do not go deep alone because you can be unable to close in and get melted.
Jayce.watch: When Jayce places Jayce E Acceleration Gate, Jayce Q Shock Blast may follow, so immediately move sideways out of its line. When he has his hammer out, watch for the leap from Jayce Q To the Skies! and the knockback from Jayce E Thundering Blow. Also avoid the first basic attack that reduces your resistances just after he switches weapons.

Urgot.combo: Use Rumble E Electro Harpoon → Rumble E Electro Harpoon → Rumble Q Flamespitter for a basic trade. Watch your Heat and activate Rumble Q Flamespitter in the Danger Zone, but account for having no way out if overheat silences you. To block Urgot’s escape route, cast Rumble R The Equalizer first, then follow with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Urgot.escape: Right after Urgot E Disdain is down is your window to close the gap. Slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, use the movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield to get in, then create distance before Urgot E Disdain becomes a threat again.
Urgot.fight: Harass Urgot with Rumble E Electro Harpoon from outside his short range until Urgot E Disdain is down. Once Urgot E Disdain is down, land both charges of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to stack the slow and magic resistance reduction, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter for a short burst of damage. If Urgot approaches with Urgot W Purge active, use the movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield to create distance instead of relying on the slow.
Urgot.laning: Hit Urgot with Rumble E Electro Harpoon when he steps forward to last-hit, and look for an angle to close in with Rumble Q Flamespitter only if Urgot E Disdain is down. Staying near Urgot too long lets damage from Urgot P Echoing Flames build up, so after trading, move outside his short range. If you’ve pushed the lane too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape in areas without vision.
Urgot.teamfight: Stay behind your frontline, watch for an engage with Urgot E Disdain, and position to catch multiple enemy frontline champions in the area of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mage deal damage. Once a fight starts, draw Rumble R The Equalizer between the enemy frontline and backline or across their escape route to block movement.
Urgot.build: Urgot’s main damage is physical, so build armor first. Urgot P Echoing Flames deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid building only large amounts of health, and also consider your total health when trying to stay above Urgot R Fear Beyond Death’s execution threshold.
Urgot.phase: In the late game, it becomes harder for Rumble to get close, so manage your distance to avoid being caught by Urgot first.
Urgot.watch: Urgot E Disdain charges in and stuns Rumble, so don’t move into range to use Rumble Q Flamespitter, which has short range, until it’s down. If Urgot Q Corrosive Charge hits you, it heavily slows you and Urgot W Purge also focuses its fire on you, so dodge Corrosive Charge when it’s thrown and use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed to create distance. If Urgot R Fear Beyond Death hits you, get completely out of Urgot’s range before you reach the execution threshold.

Volibear.combo: For a basic trade, hit Volibear twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter active. In a fight, build Heat with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If Rumble R The Equalizer is available, block Volibear’s escape route and follow the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Volibear.escape: The chance to approach comes after the stun from Volibear Q Thundering Smash has been used. If Volibear R Stormbringer is also down, you have less reason to worry about his remaining dash, so land the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and go in. If only Volibear Q Thundering Smash is down, account for his ability to escape with R Stormbringer.
Volibear.fight: If Volibear has built stacks of P The Relentless Storm by hitting minions, don’t take a fight; wait for the stacks to fall off. Step sideways out of the mark from Volibear E Sky Splitter, and manage your distance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon so you don’t get stunned by Q Thundering Smash. If you can’t finish him decisively, disengage from a long fight that would let Volibear heal with W Frenzied Maul.
Volibear.laning: Safely chip Volibear down with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then slow him when he steps up to last-hit and close in with Rumble Q Flamespitter. Don’t stand forward after using both charges of Rumble E Electro Harpoon, and if the lane is pushed without vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Volibear.teamfight: From behind your frontline, overlap Rumble Q Flamespitter on multiple enemies in the frontline, including Volibear. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mage deal damage, and draw Rumble R The Equalizer between the frontline and backline or across the enemy escape route to split their formation. Don’t fight Volibear head-on if he comes in with stacks of P The Relentless Storm.
Volibear.build: Volibear’s main abilities—Q Thundering Smash, W Frenzied Maul, and R Stormbringer—deal physical damage, so build armor first. Keep in mind that armor won’t block the magic damage from P The Relentless Storm or E Sky Splitter. If healing from Volibear W Frenzied Maul is letting him survive trades, reduce his healing with Morellonomicon.
Volibear.phase: Early on, Rumble’s low magic resistance makes Volibear P The Relentless Storm and E Sky Splitter damage a threat, so keep trades short. In the late game, Rumble can be melted before getting close, so don’t dive deep first.
Volibear.watch: Volibear Q Thundering Smash increases his movement speed as he approaches, then stuns with an empowered basic attack, so let time pass outside his basic attack range. When you see the marker for Volibear E Sky Splitter, move to the side to avoid the damage and slow. While Volibear R Stormbringer is available, don’t stay under a turret at low health.

Yasuo.combo: First remove Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield, then trade with Rumble E Electro Harpoon → Rumble E Electro Harpoon → Rumble Q Flamespitter. When using Rumble R The Equalizer, cut off his escape route, then follow with Rumble E Electro Harpoon → Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Yasuo.fight: First remove Yasuo P Way of the Wanderer’s shield with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then trade in earnest. When Yasuo steps up to last-hit or right after he throws his tornado, land the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and keep him in range of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Rumble has no skill to escape on his own, so don’t go deep where Yasuo has plenty of footholds to dash through.
Yasuo.laning: Keep the wave thin on your side of the lane to limit the footholds for Yasuo E Sweeping Blade. Usually, harass safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, and don’t activate Rumble Q Flamespitter first if you have no angle to get close. If you’ve pushed the lane too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to disengage.
Yasuo.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and catch multiple enemy frontline champions in the area of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mage deal damage. Use Rumble R The Equalizer in a fight that has already started to split the enemy frontline from the backline or block their escape route.
Yasuo.build: Yasuo’s main damage from Q Steel Tempest and R Last Breath is physical, so build armor first. Keep in mind that armor won’t block the magic damage from Yasuo E Sweeping Blade.
Yasuo.escape: Yasuo’s knock-up stacks reset just after he throws a whirlwind, so go in then. Yasuo E Sweeping Blade is a dash with a short cooldown, so don’t chase deep just because he used it once. If Yasuo R Last Breath is down, look for a chance to go in with your allies’ crowd control.
Yasuo.phase: Early on, Rumble can handle trades against a melee opponent dealing physical damage, but manage your distance so Yasuo E Sweeping Blade can’t catch you. In the late game, Rumble can’t get close and is easily melted, so avoid forcing an engage.
Yasuo.watch: Yasuo E Sweeping Blade uses minions as stepping stones to approach, so keep your distance when there are many minions. After Yasuo lands Q Steel Tempest twice in a row, watch for the knock-up from his next Q and dodge by moving sideways out of its line. If you’re knocked up, Yasuo can follow with R Last Breath.

Yone.combo: For a basic trade, hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter active. For a longer fight, watch your Heat, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you can block Yone’s escape route, cast Rumble R The Equalizer first, then follow with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Yone.escape: Your chance to go in comes after Yone’s Q tornado stacks disappear and Yone E Soul Unbound and R Fate Sealed are down. If only one movement ability is down, he can still escape with the other, so don’t force a chase. When you need to retreat, create distance with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and the movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield.
Yone.fight: While Yone’s Q tornado is ready, don’t close in; harass safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. When the tornado stacks disappear and Yone steps forward to last-hit, land the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then get into range of Rumble Q Flamespitter. When Yone goes in, manage the distance with the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield.
Yone.teamfight: Wait for Yone’s engage from behind your frontline, and position where multiple enemies can enter the range of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Place Rumble R The Equalizer between the enemy frontline and backline or across their escape route, and lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Spread out so you don’t all get hit by Yone W Spirit Cleave, and make sure you aren’t standing alone at the very back of your formation in case of Yone R Fate Sealed.
Yone.build: Prioritize movement speed so you can get out of the way of telegraphed attacks. Yone Q Mortal Steel and Yone P Way of the Hunter deal different types of damage, so don’t choose only one resistance when building defenses. Yone W Spirit Cleave deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid building only large amounts of health.
Yone.laning: Keep your distance when Yone is preparing his whirlwind Q, and don’t use Rumble Q Flamespitter first if there’s no opening to get close. If you’ve pushed the lane too far, check river vision, and in areas without vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to disengage.
Yone.phase: In the late game, Rumble can’t get close and is easily melted, so watch for Yone’s engage and fight from behind your frontline.
Yone.watch: If Yone repeatedly hits minions with Yone Q Mortal Steel to prepare his whirlwind, stay outside its dash range until the stacks disappear. If Yone closes in with Yone E Soul Unbound or uses Yone R Fate Sealed, Rumble has no mobility skill to get away on his own, making him vulnerable to follow-up attacks. If health is at around half while Yone E Soul Unbound is active, create distance in advance because additional damage comes in when he returns.

Yorick.combo: For a basic trade, hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter active. To start a fight, build Heat with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If Rumble R The Equalizer is available, cut off Yorick’s escape route, then follow with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Yorick.fight: After dodging Yorick E Mourning Mist or when it is down, slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon as you approach. Don’t start a fight where there are many graves and Mist Walkers; clear the Mist Walkers before closing in. Use Rumble W Scrap Shield as you approach after building Heat to benefit from its shield and movement speed.
Yorick.laning: Dodge the orb trajectory of Yorick E Mourning Mist, and step forward to farm while it is down. Push the lane so minions die under the enemy turret and Yorick can’t build up graves on his side. Rumble Q Flamespitter deals reduced damage to minions, so don’t spend it entirely on farming; use it after slowing Yorick with Rumble E Electro Harpoon when he steps up to last-hit.
Yorick.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and position so multiple enemies in the frontline enter the range of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mage deal damage. Use Rumble R The Equalizer to draw a line between the enemy frontline and backline or block their escape route in a fight that has already started.
Yorick.build: Yorick Q Last Rites and his ghouls’ attacks deal physical damage, so build armor first. Yorick E Mourning Mist and Yorick R Eulogy of the Isles deal magic damage based on maximum health, so be careful about building only large amounts of health. If healing from Yorick Q Last Rites offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, reduce his healing with Morellonomicon.
Yorick.escape: Yorick has no mobility skill, so engage when you dodge Yorick E Mourning Mist or while that ability is down. If you’re trapped in Yorick W Dark Procession, attack and break the wall. When you need to retreat, use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed. If Rumble overheats through Rumble P Junkyard Titan, the silence leaves him with no way to escape, so only choose to overheat in a close-range situation where a finish is certain.
Yorick.phase: Early on, Rumble can handle melee trades against Yorick’s main physical damage, but avoid Yorick E Mourning Mist and areas with many graves. In the late game, Rumble can’t get close and is easily melted, so avoid situations where you’re locked in a long fight with Yorick.
Yorick.watch: Yorick E Mourning Mist slows, marks, and deals damage based on maximum health, so dodge the ball’s trajectory first. If you get trapped in Yorick W Dark Procession, attack and break the wall. If the Maiden of the Mist summoned by Yorick R Eulogy of the Isles starts attacking you, create distance from Yorick himself.

Chogath.build: Cho’Gath’s main damage is magic and Rumble has low magic resistance, so buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads. Then fit Force of Nature between your core items to gain more time on top of him. If healing from Cho’Gath P Carnivore offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, reduce his healing with Morellonomicon.
Chogath.combo: For a basic trade, hit Cho’Gath twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter active. To start a fight, use one Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build Heat into the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you can cut off Cho’Gath’s escape route, cast Rumble R The Equalizer first, then land the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and follow with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Chogath.escape: Cho’Gath has no mobility ability, so look to engage after Cho’Gath Q Rupture has been used on the wave or after you dodge its ground marker. Also dodge the frontal area of Cho’Gath W Feral Scream, then slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and get on top of him. If Cho’Gath Q Rupture hits you, it is easy to get hit again, so manage your distance before engaging.
Chogath.fight: After Cho’Gath Q Rupture is down or you dodge its marker, move out of the frontal area of Cho’Gath W Feral Scream before starting a fight. Slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to close the gap, then watch your Heat and keep Rumble Q Flamespitter active in the Danger Zone. Use Rumble W Scrap Shield to gain a shield and movement speed as you get on top of him.
Chogath.laning: Early on, poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. When Cho’Gath steps forward to last-hit, land the slow and pressure him with Rumble Q Flamespitter. Cho’Gath E Vorpal Spikes pass through minions, so move out of the line of his basic attacks. The moment after Cho’Gath uses Cho’Gath Q Rupture on the wave is your chance to pressure him; if you push the lane too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Chogath.phase: Early on, Rumble has low magic resistance and must watch out for Cho’Gath’s magic damage, but it’s preferable to pressure the lane before Cho’Gath builds stacks. Rumble’s ability to affect other lanes improves after learning Rumble R The Equalizer, and he is strong in mid game as his ability power builds up. Later, Rumble has trouble getting on top of Cho’Gath while Cho’Gath grows stronger with stacks, so don’t give him a kill when your health is in a risky spot.
Chogath.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and position so Rumble Q Flamespitter’s cone hits several enemies in their frontline. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. In a fight that has already started, cast Rumble R The Equalizer between their frontline and backline or across their escape route to block their movement.
Chogath.watch: When you see the ground marker from Cho’Gath Q Rupture, immediately walk to the side to dodge the knock-up. Move to the side to avoid the frontal cone of Cho’Gath W Feral Scream, and if you are silenced, focus on walking rather than using abilities. If you are at or below half health, retreat out of range of Cho’Gath R Feast, which deals true damage.

Darius.build: Build armor first against Darius P Hemorrhage, Darius Q Decimate, and Darius W Crippling Strike. Darius E Apprehend penetrates some resistances, and Darius R Noxian Guillotine deals true damage, so don’t rely on armor alone to survive. If healing from Darius Q Decimate offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, cut his healing with Morellonomicon.
Darius.combo: For a basic trade, hit Darius twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter active. To start a fight, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build Heat into the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you can cut off Darius’s escape route, block it with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Darius.escape: Engage when Darius E Apprehend misses or is on cooldown. The window while Darius R Noxian Guillotine is down is also an opportunity, but if Darius P Hemorrhage stacks build up, use Rumble W Scrap Shield to create distance and end the fight.
Darius.fight: Chip away at Darius’s health with Rumble E Electro Harpoon from outside Darius E Apprehend range, and take a short trade when Apprehend misses or is down. When Darius steps forward to last-hit, land the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and get on top of him with Rumble Q Flamespitter. Before Darius P Hemorrhage stacks build up, use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed to get away and end the extended fight.
Darius.laning: Don’t use all of Rumble Q Flamespitter to farm; poke with Rumble E Electro Harpoon from outside Darius E Apprehend range. The moment after Darius uses Darius Q Decimate to clear minions is your chance to poke. If you push the lane too far, check river vision; in areas without vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Darius.phase: Early on, Rumble’s health and armor make short trades reasonable, but avoid extended fights with Darius and chaotic fights early in the game. In the late game, Rumble may struggle to get close and be burst down, so watch for Darius E Apprehend and move behind your frontline.
Darius.teamfight: Stay behind your frontline and watch the range of Darius E Apprehend while looking for a position where Rumble Q Flamespitter’s cone can hit several enemies. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. Use Rumble R The Equalizer to split their frontline from their backline or block their escape route in a fight that has already started.
Darius.watch: If Darius E Apprehend pulls you in, he follows with Darius W Crippling Strike and Darius Q Decimate, so poke from outside E range. When you see Darius Q Decimate, move outside the blade’s edge or get close to his body to reduce his healing. While Darius P Hemorrhage stacks are building, create distance; if health has dropped while stacks remain, get completely out of range of Darius R Noxian Guillotine.

DrMundo.build: Build armor first against Dr. Mundo’s main damage, Dr. Mundo E Blunt Force Trauma. If healing from Dr. Mundo P Goes Where He Pleases, Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw, and Dr. Mundo W Heart Zapper lets him survive extended fights, reduce his healing with Morellonomicon.
DrMundo.combo: For a basic trade, hit Dr. Mundo twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. To start a fight, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build Heat into the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If Rumble R The Equalizer is available, cast it across Dr. Mundo’s escape route, follow with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then get on top of him with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
DrMundo.escape: The moment after Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw is blocked by a minion or misses is your chance to engage without worrying about its slow. Dr. Mundo has no ability to create distance on his own, so engage when you have an angle to hit him twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is down. When retreating, use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s shield and movement speed.
DrMundo.fight: When Dr. Mundo steps forward to last-hit, slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then approach. Hit him twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, and keep him inside the cone of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Don’t force a kill while Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage is available again.
DrMundo.laning: Take advantage of Dr. Mundo’s low magic resistance early by safely chipping away at his health with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Dodge Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw from behind minions, and don’t use Rumble Q Flamespitter first if you don’t have an angle to get on top of him. If you push the lane too far, check river vision; if you have no vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
DrMundo.phase: Early on, Dr. Mundo’s low magic resistance makes him vulnerable to pressure from Rumble’s magic damage. His magic resistance increases greatly as he levels up, so secure an early lead. Rumble’s ability to influence other lanes increases after he learns Rumble R The Equalizer, and he is strong in mid game as his ability power builds up. In late game, however, he struggles to close in and can be killed quickly, so choose your engages carefully.
DrMundo.teamfight: From behind your frontline, find a position where Rumble Q Flamespitter can hit several enemies in their frontline, including Dr. Mundo. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. Use Rumble R The Equalizer to split their frontline from their backline or block the escape route in a fight that has started.
DrMundo.watch: Dr. Mundo Q Infected Bonesaw hits the first target it reaches and is especially painful when you are at full health, so dodge it with minions between you and him. Dr. Mundo E Blunt Force Trauma empowers his basic attacks, so don’t take repeated hits at close range. If Dr. Mundo activates Dr. Mundo R Maximum Dosage, his healing and movement speed increase, so don’t spend too long trying to kill him.

Fiora.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Fiora Q Lunge and Fiora E Bladework. If an extended duel lets the healing from Fiora P Duelist’s Dance and Fiora R Grand Challenge offset Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, reduce her healing with Morellonomicon.
Fiora.combo: For a basic trade, hit Fiora twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter active. To start a fight, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build Heat into the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you use your ultimate, block her escape route with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and hit her with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Fiora.escape: Immediately after you make Fiora use Fiora Q Lunge is Rumble’s chance to close the gap. After Fiora W Riposte is down, hit her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and engage; when disengaging, use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed. While overheated, the silence prevents you from using abilities to escape, so manage your Heat in fights you can’t finish.
Fiora.fight: Use the moment Fiora engages with Fiora Q Lunge as a chance to counterattack, but don’t use all your key attacks at once if Fiora W Riposte is available. Slow her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then control the distance with Rumble W Scrap Shield’s shield and movement speed while keeping her in range of Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Fiora.laning: Stand opposite her vital and poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Trade briefly when Fiora steps forward to last-hit or just after she uses Fiora Q Lunge, and don’t chase recklessly. If you’ve pushed the lane and have no river vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Fiora.phase: Early on, Rumble’s health and armor let him take physical melee trades with Fiora.
Fiora.teamfight: Position behind your frontline so Fiora and several other enemies can enter Rumble Q Flamespitter’s range. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, and cast Rumble R The Equalizer between their frontline and backline or across their escape route to block their movement. If Fiora R Grand Challenge targets you, stand against a wall so she can’t reach all four vitals.
Fiora.watch: When a vital from Fiora P Duelist’s Dance appears, stand on the opposite side to narrow the angle of Fiora Q Lunge’s engage. Fiora W Riposte can negate attacks, so move to the side as you activate Rumble Q Flamespitter to avoid its counterattack. If Fiora R Grand Challenge hits you, stand against a wall to block one side’s vital.

Gangplank.build: Build armor early in lane to counter the physical damage from Gangplank Q Parrrley and Gangplank E Powder Keg. If the healing from Gangplank W Remove Scurvy offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, reduce his healing with Morellonomicon. Gangplank P Trial by Fire and Gangplank R Cannon Barrage deal true damage, which resistances cannot mitigate, so factor in your total health as well.
Gangplank.combo: For a standard trade, hit both shots of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to stack the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on him. To start a fight, check your Heat, use one shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. When using Rumble R The Equalizer, cut off Gangplank’s escape route, then follow up with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Gangplank.escape: Engage just after Gangplank E Powder Keg is placed, if there are no aged kegs nearby. Once Gangplank W Remove Scurvy is down, Rumble E Electro Harpoon’s slow makes him easier to catch. Gangplank has no skill that creates distance on its own, but if you have pushed in an area without vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Gangplank.fight: Your chance to trade comes just after Gangplank E Powder Keg is placed, while it is still fresh. Slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield to close in and keep him within Rumble Q Flamespitter’s range. Back away first if there is an aged keg nearby.
Gangplank.laning: Poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then look for a chance to close in when Gangplank steps forward to last-hit. If Gangplank E Powder Keg is placed nearby, destroy it from outside its range and avoid fighting around an aged keg. If you have pushed too far, check river vision; in areas without vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Gangplank.phase: Early on, Rumble can trade reasonably well with a physical melee opponent, but build armor early so Gangplank Q Parrrley’s poke does not add up. Rumble is strongest in mid game as his ability power builds; avoid forcing fights up close in late game.
Gangplank.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and find a position where Rumble Q Flamespitter’s cone can hit multiple enemies. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. Use Rumble R The Equalizer in an ongoing fight to split the enemy frontline from the backline or block their escape route.
Gangplank.watch: Gangplank E Powder Keg gets more dangerous as it ages, so destroy it from outside its blast radius and back away from an aged keg or a spot where two kegs overlap. Gangplank P Trial by Fire deals true damage and grants movement speed, and Gangplank R Cannon Barrage also slows and deals true damage, so be careful when your health is low.

Garen.build: Build armor first to counter the physical damage from Garen Q Decisive Strike and Garen E Judgment. Garen R Demacian Justice cannot be reduced by resistances, so factor in your total health as well. If the healing from Garen P Perseverance offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, reduce his healing with Morellonomicon.
Garen.combo: For a standard trade, hit both shots of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to stack the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on him. To start a fight, use the first shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build Heat and enter Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. Delay your combo by half a beat when Garen W Courage activates; when using your ultimate, block his escape route with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow up with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Garen.escape: Garen has no mobility skill, so the moment after Garen Q Decisive Strike’s empowered attack is used is your chance to engage. Close in with Rumble E Electro Harpoon’s slow, but avoid a long fight once Garen E Judgment starts spinning and use Rumble W Scrap Shield to create distance.
Garen.fight: Trade briefly just after Garen Q Decisive Strike’s empowered attack is used. Slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to make up for Rumble Q Flamespitter’s short range, and avoid staying in Garen E Judgment’s spin for too long. Wait out the brief moment when Garen W Courage grants a shield and tenacity, then use your combo.
Garen.laning: Poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon from the start, and pressure Garen with Rumble Q Flamespitter when he steps up to last-hit. Limit the time he has to build stacks on Garen W Courage, but check river vision if you have pushed too far. In areas without vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Garen.phase: Early on, use your trades against a physical melee opponent to limit Garen’s growth. In late game, Rumble has a harder time closing in while Garen W Courage’s stacks remain, so avoid forcing close-range fights.
Garen.teamfight: Position behind your frontline where Rumble Q Flamespitter can hit several enemies in their frontline, including Garen. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage, and place Rumble R The Equalizer between their frontline and backline or along their escape route to restrict their movement.
Garen.watch: Garen Q Decisive Strike’s empowered attack silences you, so do not approach first while he has it ready. Staying in Garen E Judgment’s spin for too long is costly, so use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed to get out. If your health is below half, stay out of range of Garen R Demacian Justice, which deals true damage based on your missing health.

Gnar.build: Build armor first to counter Gnar’s main source of damage. Gnar W Hyper / Wallop deals magic damage and damage based on your maximum health, so do not expect armor or health alone to block it all. Rumble has no mobility skill, so prioritize tenacity if the stun from Gnar R GNAR! is a threat.
Gnar.combo: For a standard trade, hit both shots of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to stack the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on him. To start a fight, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build Heat and enter Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you can block Gnar’s escape route, cut it off with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow up with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Gnar.escape: The moment after Gnar E Hop / Crunch is used is your window to engage. If Gnar R GNAR! is also down, you can close in near a wall with less risk of being knocked into it and stunned. Use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield when engaging or retreating.
Gnar.fight: When Mini Gnar steps forward to last-hit, slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and close in. You have an opening to close the distance immediately after you make Gnar use Gnar E Hop / Crunch. Avoid fighting Mega Gnar head-on right after he transforms, and fight aggressively after he returns to Mini Gnar, while he cannot transform again.
Gnar.laning: Use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to safely answer Mini Gnar’s ranged poke, and do not activate Rumble Q Flamespitter first when you have no opening to close in. Avoid the path of Gnar Q Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss and prevent Gnar from catching his boomerang to buy time before his next poke. If the lane is pushed and you lack river vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Gnar.phase: Early on, Mini Gnar pokes Rumble from range, but his health is low, so trade only when you can close in. In late game, do not force your way in; fight from behind your frontline.
Gnar.teamfight: Watch Gnar’s Rage and look to fight just after he changes from Mega Gnar back to Mini Gnar. Do not stand with a wall at your back or between Gnar and a wall. Use Rumble R The Equalizer to split the enemy frontline from the backline or block their escape route. From behind your frontline, hit multiple enemies with Rumble Q Flamespitter and lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage.
Gnar.watch: The boomerang from Gnar Q Boomerang Throw / Boulder Toss can also hit you on its return, so move out of its path and prevent Gnar from catching it. Back away when Mega Gnar gets close, and do not let a wall be at your back. Gnar R GNAR! stuns you if it knocks you into a wall, so do not stand between Gnar and a wall.

Gwen.build: Use Null-Magic Mantle to withstand the early game and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Gwen’s main damage is magic, and Rumble has low magic resistance, so fit Force of Nature between your core items to buy time in close range. If the healing from Gwen P A Thousand Cuts offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, reduce her healing with Morellonomicon.
Gwen.combo: For a standard trade, hit both shots of Rumble E Electro Harpoon in succession to stack the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on her. For an extended fight, check your Heat, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. When using Rumble R The Equalizer, cut off Gwen’s escape route, then follow with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and close in with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Gwen.escape: Immediately after you make Gwen use Gwen E Skip 'n Slash is your window to close the distance. Gwen E Skip 'n Slash gets much of its cooldown back if it hits something, so avoid chasing where there are many minions; close in with Rumble E Electro Harpoon’s slow on terrain without minions. Use Rumble W Scrap Shield to disengage when the slow from Gwen R Needlework is a threat.
Gwen.fight: Trade briefly when Gwen steps forward to last-hit, before Gwen Q Snip Snip! has built stacks. Slow her first with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield to keep Gwen in the cone of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Move to avoid the center of Gwen Q Snip Snip!, and do not let Gwen keep basic attacking you for long.
Gwen.laning: Early on, avoid forcing close fights because Rumble has low magic resistance, and poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. If you have pushed the lane, check river vision; in areas without vision, save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Gwen.phase: However, before Gwen Q Snip Snip! has built stacks, you have a chance to trade, so hit her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and fight briefly.
Gwen.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and position in front of the enemy frontline where Rumble Q Flamespitter’s cone can hit multiple enemies. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage, and place Rumble R The Equalizer between the enemy frontline and backline or along their escape route. Avoid the center of Gwen Q Snip Snip!, and do not try to target Gwen from outside the mist while she is inside Gwen W Hallowed Mist.
Gwen.watch: The center of Gwen Q Snip Snip!’s cone deals heavy true damage, so move sideways to avoid it. Gwen P A Thousand Cuts and Gwen R Needlework deal damage based on your maximum health, and Gwen R Needlework also slows, so be careful in extended close fights. When Gwen W Hallowed Mist is active, you cannot target her from outside the mist, so enter it or wait for it to end.

Illaoi.build: If the healing from Illaoi P Prophet of an Elder God offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, reduce her healing with Morellonomicon. Build armor first to counter Illaoi’s main damage. Illaoi W Harsh Lesson deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid an item choice that greatly increases health alone.
Illaoi.combo: For a standard trade, hit both shots of Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on her. In a fight, check your Heat, use Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. When using your ultimate, cut off her escape route with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and hit her with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Illaoi.escape: Your chance to engage comes just after you dodge Illaoi E Test of Spirit and Illaoi W Harsh Lesson is used. Close in with Rumble E Electro Harpoon’s slow and use Rumble W Scrap Shield’s movement speed to get on her. If there are many tentacles nearby, do not go in deep even then.
Illaoi.fight: Close in after dodging Illaoi E Test of Spirit or just after making Illaoi use Illaoi W Harsh Lesson. Slow her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter and keep the damage going by moving and turning with her. Do not take a fight near a wall where tentacles have spawned.
Illaoi.laning: Keep the lane position away from walls and last-hit outside Illaoi E Test of Spirit’s range. Poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon; when Illaoi steps forward to last-hit, land the slow and trade with Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you have pushed too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to disengage.
Illaoi.phase: Early on, Rumble can trade reasonably well with a physical melee opponent, but you must dodge Illaoi E Test of Spirit and the tentacles near walls. In late game, Rumble may be unable to close in and can be melted, so avoid forcing an engage.
Illaoi.teamfight: Do not group up before Illaoi R Leap of Faith; if she uses it, spread out and wait out its duration. Destroy the tentacles or draw Illaoi into open ground away from walls. From behind your frontline, hit multiple enemies with Rumble Q Flamespitter, lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, and block their escape route with Rumble R The Equalizer.
Illaoi.watch: Prioritize dodging Illaoi E Test of Spirit. If it hits, fight back if you can; if you cannot, break the tether and dodge the first tentacle. When Illaoi R Leap of Faith is active, do not stay near the tentacles; create distance.

Irelia.build: If the healing from Irelia Q Bladesurge offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter’s damage over time, consider Morellonomicon first. The source material does not specify Irelia’s damage types, so it is not possible to determine which resistance to build.
Irelia.combo: Manage your Heat so you have room to activate Rumble Q Flamespitter in Danger Zone. Hit both shots of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to stack the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on her. When using your ultimate, block her escape route with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow up with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Irelia.escape: Immediately after you make Irelia use Irelia Q Bladesurge is Rumble’s chance to close the distance. If Irelia E Flawless Duet’s stun is also down, land Rumble E Electro Harpoon’s slow and engage.
Irelia.fight: Start a fight when Irelia steps up to last-hit or just after Irelia Q Bladesurge is used. Slow her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield to close in and keep her within Rumble Q Flamespitter’s range.
Irelia.laning: Usually, poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon; if a low-health minion appears between you and Irelia, back away. If you have pushed too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape.
Irelia.phase: In late game, avoid forcing an engage because it is difficult to close in.
Irelia.teamfight: Prioritize Irelia from behind your frontline and position so Rumble Q Flamespitter hits several enemies. Use Rumble R The Equalizer to split the enemy frontline from the backline or block their escape route, and lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage.
Irelia.watch: Irelia can repeatedly approach by using Irelia Q Bladesurge on low-health minions, so keep your distance when minions are about to die. Avoid the stun from Irelia E Flawless Duet, and if you are trapped inside Irelia R Vanguard’s Edge, wait for the blades to disappear.

Jax.build: Jax stacks damage through basic attacks and attack speed, so prioritize defenses that reduce attack speed. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so build both armor and magic resistance instead of heavily stacking health alone. If magic damage is the main threat, fit Force of Nature between your core items.
Jax.combo: For a standard trade, hit both shots of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to stack the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on him. To fight aggressively, use one shot of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If Rumble R The Equalizer is available, place it along Jax’s escape route, then follow up with Rumble E Electro Harpoon’s slow and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Jax.escape: The moment after Jax Q Leap Strike is used is a window to close the distance because his mobility is down. If Jax E Counter Strike also ends and you avoid the stun, slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and engage. When you need to retreat, use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield, and avoid situations where Overheat’s silence prevents you from using an escape skill.
Jax.fight: While Jax E Counter Strike is down, slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and keep him in Rumble Q Flamespitter’s range. When Jax E Counter Strike is active, stop basic attacking and back away. When you fight again, set your Heat to Danger Zone and activate Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Jax.laning: If you have pushed too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape when there is no vision.
Jax.teamfight: When Jax jumps in with Jax E Counter Strike active, spread out so you are not all hit by the area stun, then concentrate your skills after the stun ends. From behind your frontline, hit multiple enemies with Rumble Q Flamespitter and lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Place Rumble R The Equalizer between the enemy frontline and backline or along their escape route to split their formation.
Jax.watch: Jax E Counter Strike negates basic attacks and, when reactivated, deals damage based on maximum health and stuns enemies in an area. When Jax E Counter Strike is active, stop basic attacking and move out of its stun range. Save Rumble W Scrap Shield for when he closes in with Jax Q Leap Strike.

Kayle.build: Early on, withstand Kayle's magic damage with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. If you still don't have enough time to stay close and fight, fit Force of Nature between your core items. If the healing from Kayle W Celestial Blessing offsets Rumble Q Flamespitter's damage over time, reduce her healing with Morellonomicon.
Kayle.combo: Your basic trade is to hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to amplify its slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on. To start a fight, build heat with Rumble E Electro Harpoon until you enter the Danger Zone, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. When using Rumble R The Equalizer, cut off Kayle's escape route, then follow with the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and hit her with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Kayle.escape: Kayle has no mobility skill, so you can avoid the slow and magic resistance reduction by dodging Kayle Q Radiant Blast before approaching. If she uses Kayle W Celestial Blessing to speed up and retreat, hit twice in a row with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to amplify the slow and get within range of Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Kayle.fight: When Kayle steps up to last-hit, slow her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then get close. Watch your heat, activate Rumble Q Flamespitter in the Danger Zone, and move to keep Kayle in range while lining up your direction. Leave room in your heat bar to avoid the silence from overheating unless you're close enough to finish her for certain.
Kayle.laning: However, Rumble is also vulnerable to magic damage early, so withstand it with a Null-Magic Mantle and safely poke with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. If you've pushed the lane too far, check river vision, and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape when you have no vision.
Kayle.teamfight: Engage from behind your allied frontline and position so multiple enemies overlap within Rumble Q Flamespitter's range. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage too. Use Rumble R The Equalizer in an ongoing fight to block Kayle's escape route or split the enemy frontline and backline. If you get an opening to reach Kayle, coordinate with your allies' crowd control and timing, then focus your damage after Kayle R Divine Judgment's invulnerability ends.
Kayle.watch: Avoid being hit directly by Kayle Q Radiant Blast, which slows and reduces magic resistance. When health has decreased, watch out for Kayle E Starfire Spellblade, which deals damage based on missing health. While Kayle R Divine Judgment is active, don't commit your damage; hold her with Rumble E Electro Harpoon's slow and attack after her invulnerability ends.

Malphite.build: Malphite's main damage is magic and Rumble has low magic resistance, so buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for your boots. Fit Force of Nature between your core items to buy time to stay close and deal damage.
Malphite.combo: Your basic trade is to hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to amplify its slow and magic resistance reduction, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you can keep the fight going, use the first harpoon to build heat into the Danger Zone, then activate Q to deal more damage. If Rumble R The Equalizer is available, block Malphite's escape route, then follow with E's slow and Q.
Malphite.escape: After Malphite Q Seismic Shard hits and slows you, don't go in immediately. Use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield as you approach.
Malphite.fight: Break Malphite P Granite Shield first with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then poke at short intervals so the shield can't come back. When Malphite steps up to last-hit, slow him and approach, moving to keep hitting him for the full duration of Rumble Q Flamespitter, which deals damage based on max health.
Malphite.laning: Malphite Q Seismic Shard can't be dodged from behind minions, so don't stay in range for long. If you've pushed the lane, check river vision, and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape when you have no vision.
Malphite.teamfight: Spread out from your allies so Malphite R Unstoppable Force doesn't knock up multiple champions, and have Rumble engage from behind your allied frontline. Position to catch multiple enemy frontline champions in Rumble Q Flamespitter, and lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Place Rumble R The Equalizer between the enemy frontline and backline or across their escape route, then focus your counterattack right after Malphite R is down.
Malphite.watch: Malphite Q Seismic Shard slows you, so don't start a trade immediately after it hits. Malphite R Unstoppable Force is an unstoppable dash that can knock up multiple champions, so spread out from your allies when you can't see his position, and don't give him an angle near walls or bushes.

Nasus.build: Nasus's main damage comes from Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, so build armor first. Armor won't stop the magic damage from Nasus E Spirit Fire and Nasus R Fury of the Sands, so focus on leaving the area and keeping your distance while his ultimate is active.
Nasus.combo: Your basic trade is to hit twice in a row with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. Watch your heat, use Rumble Q Flamespitter in the Danger Zone, and turn as you move to keep Nasus in range. If you have an angle to block Nasus's escape route, cut it off with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Nasus.escape: Look to engage when Nasus W Wither is down and Nasus steps forward to last-hit. Nasus has no way to create distance on his own besides Flash, so don't hesitate to pressure him when Rumble E Electro Harpoon's slow gives you an opening to get close. Keep your distance while Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active unless you have a clear advantage.
Nasus.fight: Use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield when getting close, and don't force a continued fight when Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active.
Nasus.laning: Pressure Nasus where he can stack Nasus Q Siphoning Strike, but don't push the lane all the way under his turret and let him last-hit safely. Let the lane come toward you to punish Nasus when he steps up to last-hit or to call for a jungle gank. If you've pushed the lane too far, check river vision, and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to escape where you have no vision.
Nasus.phase: Nasus's Nasus Q Siphoning Strike stacks build over time, and Rumble has trouble getting close in the late game, so make use of your opportunities early.
Nasus.teamfight: Engage from behind your allied frontline and catch multiple enemy frontline champions in Rumble Q Flamespitter's range. Lower Nasus's magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages too. When Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active, don't face him head-on; keep your distance. Use Rumble R The Equalizer to block the enemy's escape route or split their frontline and backline.
Nasus.watch: Nasus Q Siphoning Strike gets stronger as he stacks it with last-hits, so deny him opportunities to stack from early on. If you're caught alone by Nasus W Wither, it's difficult to get away, so don't move alone within its range. Your armor is reduced while you're on Nasus E Spirit Fire, so leave the area. When Nasus R Fury of the Sands is active, avoid fighting and wait it out unless you have a clear numbers or damage advantage.

Olaf.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Olaf Q Undertow. However, Olaf Q Undertow reduces your armor when it hits, and resistances can't reduce the true damage from Olaf E Reckless Swing, so build health too. There are no specific items listed, so no further purchase order is specified.
Olaf.combo: Check your heat before the fight, then use one cast of Rumble E Electro Harpoon to enter the Danger Zone. Hit with Rumble E Electro Harpoon once more to amplify its slow and magic resistance reduction, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter and keep Olaf in range. After Olaf R Ragnarok ends, block his escape route with Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow with Rumble E Electro Harpoon → Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Olaf.escape: The window to try to approach with Rumble E Electro Harpoon is after you dodge Olaf Q Undertow and while he can't pick up his axe. Olaf has no skill that lets him create distance, but Rumble's slow doesn't work during Olaf R Ragnarok, so engage after it ends.
Olaf.fight: Dodge Olaf Q Undertow and prevent him from picking up his axe, then safely chip away at his health with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. When Olaf steps up to last-hit, hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to stack its slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on as you move. Even at low health, Olaf gains attack speed and lifesteal, so don't stay close too long.
Olaf.laning: Early on, avoid fighting Olaf directly and poke with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Move opposite the direction where Olaf Q Undertow's axe lands to stop him from picking it up. If Rumble Q Flamespitter pushes the lane too far, check river vision, and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to disengage where you have no vision.
Olaf.phase: Olaf is strong early, so don't give him a kill; survive with Rumble E Electro Harpoon's range. Olaf becomes relatively weaker later, but Rumble also has trouble getting close, so avoid reckless close-range fights.
Olaf.teamfight: Engage from behind your allied frontline and move so multiple enemies enter the cone of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Lower Olaf's magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage too. If Olaf R Ragnarok is active, create distance. Use Rumble R The Equalizer between the enemy frontline and backline or across their escape route.
Olaf.watch: If you're hit by Olaf Q Undertow, you'll be slowed and your armor will be reduced, so move away from where the axe lands to stop him from picking it up. Olaf E Reckless Swing deals true damage that resistances can't reduce, so when your health is low, use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield to create distance. Olaf R Ragnarok makes him immune to slows, and its duration extends each time he takes a hit, so don't try to hold him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon; retreat behind your allies.

Ornn.build: Rumble has no mobility spell and is easy to lock down with Ornn’s crowd control, so consider tenacity first. Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture and Ornn E Searing Charge deal physical damage, while Ornn W Bellows Breath and Ornn R Call of the Forge God deal magic damage, so build resistances without leaning too heavily toward one type. Ornn W Bellows Breath deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid stacking health alone.
Ornn.combo: For a basic trade, hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon, then activate Rumble Q Flamespitter. If you can extend the fight, build Heat with Rumble E Electro Harpoon until you enter the Danger Zone, then use the empowered Rumble Q Flamespitter. To cut off Ornn’s escape, cast Rumble R The Equalizer first, then follow the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon and keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on him.
Ornn.escape: Don’t go in deep after Ornn E Searing Charge is down if Ornn R Call of the Forge God is still available. In particular, wait for an opening where Ornn R Call of the Forge God is unavailable and you’ve dodged Ornn E Searing Charge and his crowd control; then slow him with Rumble E Electro Harpoon and move in. Save Rumble W Scrap Shield if you need a way out.
Ornn.fight: Poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon first. When Ornn steps forward to last-hit, slow him with the second Rumble E Electro Harpoon to get into Rumble Q Flamespitter range. Use the movement speed and shield from Rumble W Scrap Shield, but don’t move toward a pillar from Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture or a wall.
Ornn.laning: Pressure Ornn with Rumble E Electro Harpoon while his early damage is low. If he tries to craft an item in lane, move up and interrupt him. Don’t use all of Rumble Q Flamespitter to farm or activate it early when you have no angle to get close. If you’ve pushed the lane too far, check river vision and save Rumble W Scrap Shield to disengage when you lack vision.
Ornn.phase: Ornn’s damage is low early, giving Rumble a chance to get ahead in lane, but watch out for Ornn W Bellows Breath given Rumble’s low magic resistance. It becomes harder for Rumble to get close later, so use your early lead before Ornn’s items and allied Masterwork upgrades stack up.
Ornn.teamfight: Engage from behind your frontline and position so multiple enemies in their frontline are in range of Rumble Q Flamespitter. Lower their magic resistance with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to help your allied mages deal damage. Cast Rumble R The Equalizer between their frontline and backline, or along their escape route, to restrict movement. When you see Ornn R Call of the Forge God, move off the straight line between Ornn and the spirit, and avoid its return path too.
Ornn.watch: Near the pillar from Ornn Q Volcanic Rupture or a wall, Ornn E Searing Charge can knock you up, so back toward open space. If the final burst of Ornn W Bellows Breath makes you Brittle, don’t move forward; keep your distance until the effect ends. Even after sidestepping the spirit from Ornn R Call of the Forge God, watch for its return path.

Pantheon.build: Build armor first to withstand Pantheon’s main damage. Avoid stacking health alone because Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on your maximum health.
Pantheon.combo: For a basic trade, hit twice with Rumble E Electro Harpoon to build up the slow and magic resistance reduction, then keep Rumble Q Flamespitter on him. Before a fight, check your Heat so you can activate Rumble Q Flamespitter in the Danger Zone. To cut off Pantheon’s escape, cast Rumble R The Equalizer, then follow the slow from Rumble E Electro Harpoon with Rumble Q Flamespitter.
Pantheon.escape: Once Pantheon W Shield Vault is down, you have an opening to go in without worrying about its stun. If Pantheon R Grand Starfall is still available, he can use it to escape, so look for a sure fight when both mobility abilities are down. If the fight turns unfavorable, use the movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield to create distance.
Pantheon.fight: Pantheon is strong in early trades, so poke safely with Rumble E Electro Harpoon. Once Pantheon W Shield Vault is down and Rumble E Electro Harpoon lets you close the gap, use the shield and movement speed from Rumble W Scrap Shield to move in. If Pantheon E Aegis Assault is active, wait for it to end instead of unloading damage from the front.
